title: Emergency suspension of an Agent Artifact is reversible and must be followed by a formal review
content:
A.1.14.1.5.4 creates a bypass around the Notice-and-cure protocol: in an emergency situation "Sky Core has the discretion to immediately suspend an Agent Artifact provision or function if it reasonably suspects that the Artifact is contributing towards a significant or system-level risk," subject to a duty to "act in good faith when exercising its discretion."

The threshold is intentionally low — *reasonably suspects*, not establishes — because waiting for proof during a system-level event defeats the purpose. What keeps that low bar acceptable is that the resulting action is weak. A.1.14.1.5.4.1 provides that a suspended provision "will remain inactive until either the emergency situation is resolved or a formal review by the Core Facilitator concludes that there is no issue with the Agent Artifact." Nothing is destroyed; the provision is paused with two independent routes back to life.

A.1.14.1.5.4.2 makes the review mandatory rather than optional: any use of the emergency discretion "must be followed by a formal review process by the Core Facilitator as to the particular risks or issues with the Agent Artifact in question," which must be "timely and clearly communicated to the affected Prime Agent."

The pairing is the point. Low evidentiary bar plus reversible effect plus compulsory after-the-fact review is a coherent package: Sky Core can stop harm on suspicion, but cannot use suspicion to permanently rewrite an Agent's governance, and every exercise generates a review that either vindicates or ends the suspension.
description: Sky Core may suspend a provision on reasonable suspicion of system-level risk, but it stays merely inactive until the emergency resolves or review clears it — suspension is not invalidation.
